content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The FAD's path from \"nine incidents in a 21-month period\" and \"only two\" direct engagements to \"not severe or pervasive\" is stated, but the nine incidents are not enumerated in the record, and the finding of no basis for management liability has no stated reasoning."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most characterizations are attributed to \"Complainant stated,\" and the Business Office Manager's remarks come second-hand via instant message and an unnamed \"employee,\" while the FAD's reliance on \"witness statements\" cites no identified witnesses or ROI exhibits."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Several events are dated (Dec 11 and 13, 2017; Jan 25, 2018; June 27, 2018 filing), but the CEO's four reports are undated, the \"June or July 2018\" event is approximate, and the ROI, FAD, and any management responses or prior escalations have no dates."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The record does not name who made the FAD determination or state the standard applied beyond \"severe or pervasive,\" and it does not show that the CEO's or Deputy Director's responses were considered, only that management was found not liable."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"The record is a secondary background summary that cites an ROI and witness statements without including them, so an independent reviewer could not assess whether the FAD conclusions are supported without outside materials."}},"remediation_note":"The record would need the ROI and witness statements attached or specifically referenced, an itemized dated list of the nine incidents with their sources, and dates for the complaint steps, the ROI, and the FAD. It would also need to identify the decision-maker, state the criteria applied, and document the management responses considered, including the reasoning on liability."}
